metadata.title: ARC Prize GPT-6 Astra evaluation
metadata.description: Independent ARC-AGI-3 standard-harness, provider-adapter, and action-efficiency evaluation of GPT-6 Astra.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra on ARC-AGI-3
sources.notes: ARC Prize separately reports a standard harness and OpenAI's provider adapter, plus human-normalized action efficiency.

update.method: agent-assisted primary-source extraction and normalization with human review
update.notes: Keep standard and provider-adapter harnesses separate; do not treat either percentage as a Personal-AI delegation rate.

results.summary: 4 explicit numeric measurement(s); 0 item(s) affect the countdown.

measurements.subject: GPT-6 Astra · ARC Prize standard harness
measurements.caveat: Independent standard-harness result at maximum effort; reported evaluation cost was $26,098. Kept separate from the provider-adapter result.

measurements.subject: GPT-6 Astra · OpenAI provider adapter
measurements.caveat: Independent benchmark-operator result using OpenAI's provider adapter with persisted opaque reasoning and compaction; reported evaluation cost was $18,817. Not a direct delegation percentage.

measurements.metric: ARC-AGI-3 levels using fewer actions than median human
measurements.subject: GPT-6 Astra · OpenAI provider adapter
measurements.caveat: ARC Prize's action-efficiency comparison across evaluated levels; it supports model-level planning efficiency but does not measure household delegation directly.

measurements.metric: Mean action reduction versus median human
measurements.subject: GPT-6 Astra · OpenAI provider adapter
measurements.caveat: Average action reduction reported by ARC Prize. It is a mechanistic efficiency signal, not a direct economic completion score.

record.summary: Astra scored 62.7% on ARC Prize's standard harness and 99.9% with the provider adapter, while using fewer actions than the median human on 96.0% of levels.
